data.content_ref: inline:The alleged abstraction is refuted by its own test: SRC_004 treats the sufficiency condition as a *global* modal property — it must hold under arbitrary world-substitution with no structural preconditions connecting old and new worlds — while SRC_002's guard only makes sense once a world IS the author's own mutated descendant (same lineage, same subject identity carried through the mutation). Take a compile.py run where the surviving artifact and its acceptance test exist but the input world was replaced wholesale with an unrelated, non-author-derived world: SRC_004's 'test is sufficient iff it accepts only the surviving subject' can be evaluated and hold for that artifact, yet SRC_002's reflexive guard cannot even be instantiated because there is no self-referential (author -> own output) relation to guard. That is exactly the configuration the target says refutes it: the sufficiency condition holds while the reflexive guard fails to instantiate it — so SRC_002 is the disjoint, mutation-conditioned case SRC_004 was generalized away from, not a special case of it.
